# Shared forensic controls

## Purpose
Shared accounting control contracts, canonical operation material and authenticated transaction context. MCP and REST adapters must use the same executing services. The programme ledger records which enforcement paths are implemented; types alone do not enforce accounting controls.

## Caller contract
- Obtain ControlTx with requireControlTx inside withAuth/withBearerAuth; assertControlTx rejects forged or escaped transaction contexts.
- ControlPrincipal comes from authenticated middleware, never tool/body arguments. Person identity differs from token/grant identity.
- Current permissions must be rechecked by executing services; grantedScopes is only a ceiling.
- Keep all financial effects, operation versions and committed change evidence in one transaction/savepoint. A controlWriteFailed flag prevents middleware COMMIT even if the handler catches a failure.

## Main interfaces
- contracts.ts: ControlPrincipal, ControlTx, OperationBinding, OperationApproval, ChangeEventInput, ControlCheckResult.
- canonical.ts: canonicalJson rejects lossy evidence; canonicalMoney preserves bounded decimal precision; operationBindingHash normalizes and binds all material facts.
- bindingValidation.ts validates dates, positive versions, policy and beneficiary/source references before hashing.
- context.ts creates immutable authenticated principals and binds control contexts to the live ALS client.

## Business rules
- Tenant predicates on every tenant query, tagged SQL only. Unknown authority fails closed.
- Each applicable policy must pass; person separation is based on users.id, not token inequality.
- Sort set-valued references by fixed code-unit order; do not use locale collation for signatures.
- Never put plaintext bank/payroll secrets or tokens into generic audit output.
- Legacy missing provenance stays unknown; do not fabricate historical evidence.
- Retained rows are matched by canonical entity identity: `lower(entity_id)` within `company_id`, and result identities compared with `sameIntentId`. A receipt read (`loadIntentReceipt`) refuses two spellings of one receipt.
- A retained spelling is a lineage, and a fork (two spellings of one entity) is two lineages. Writers and projections follow one rule, `lineageChoice`/`retainedLineage`: the most advanced lineage (highest version), the canonical lowercase spelling on a tie; a tie with no canonical spelling refuses for writers and is flagged by projections. That lineage holds the entity's current state and its version-keyed rows (payroll calculation versions), so extending another strands real work. The caller's spelling never decides. The change event and protected evidence are written under the lineage the version row keeps.
- Callers that read versions with their own query (bankRuleChangeControl, glAccountChangeControl, glMergeChangeControl, defaultAccountsControl) match `lower(entity_id)` and choose through `retainedLineage`, so the version read and the row extended are always the same lineage.
- Projections that report evidence (audit snapshot sources, risk and three-way-match queries, payroll control) join versions through a `LATERAL ... ORDER BY version DESC, canonical first LIMIT 1`, and receipts through one that prefers the receipt that consumed the approval — never a bare equality on `lower(entity_id)`, which returns a forked entity twice, kills the snapshot job and inflates risk populations. A forked snapshot record carries `control_lineage_forked: true` and a twinned attestation receipt `control_receipt_twinned: true` (only those records; others are unchanged), with `forked_lineage:<source>` / `twinned_receipt:<source>` in coverage; statement completeness flags `receiptTwinned`. Transaction evidence flags `forked` and records `CONTROL_LINEAGE_FORKED`, or `CONTROL_LINEAGE_AMBIGUOUS` when no lineage can be followed. Detectors (journal risk) never pick a lineage: they read change history across every retained spelling and name the fork (`change_history_lineage_forked`), so no signal depends on the spelling an edit was recorded under. Change history never merges lineages: on a fork it answers `FORKED_LINEAGE` with each lineage and `writerLineage` (the one the next write extends), and each lineage is read, paged and cursored by name; a cursor minted before lineage selection is refused on a fork.
- Max 300 lines per implementation file; root owns shared contracts and migration allocation.
